The time columns of weeks and of isoyears

Source: R/synthetic_grid.R
synthetic_weeks.Rd

synthetic_weeks() returns one row for each isoyearweek from from to to. synthetic_years() returns one row for each isoyear of those weeks.

Usage

synthetic_weeks(from, to)

synthetic_years(from, to)

Arguments

from, to

The first and the last isoyearweek, as text, for example "2021-30".

Value

A data.table with the 12 time columns.

Details

Each function returns the 12 time columns of csfmt_rts_data_v2: granularity_time, isoyearweek, isoyear, isoweek, isoquarter, isoyearquarter, season, seasonweek, date, calyear, calmonth and calyearmonth. cstime derives each column except granularity_time from isoyearweek. date is the last date of the week, and calyear, calmonth and calyearmonth come from date. The integer columns are integer, seasonweek is numeric, and date is a Date.

synthetic_weeks() sets granularity_time to "isoyearweek". synthetic_years() sets it to "isoyear". A row of synthetic_years() takes the last isoyearweek of its isoyear, from cstime::isoyear_to_last_isoyearweek_c(). That week can be after to.

Put the result in the world as a data.frame element. Then synthetic_grid_generator() gives each table the time columns that it holds.

Examples

synthetic_weeks("2021-30", "2021-32")
#>    granularity_time isoyearweek isoyear isoweek isoquarter isoyearquarter
#>              <char>      <char>   <int>   <int>      <int>         <char>
#> 1:      isoyearweek     2021-30    2021      30          3        2021-Q3
#> 2:      isoyearweek     2021-31    2021      31          3        2021-Q3
#> 3:      isoyearweek     2021-32    2021      32          3        2021-Q3
#>       season seasonweek       date calyear calmonth calyearmonth
#>       <char>      <num>     <Date>   <int>    <int>       <char>
#> 1: 2021/2022         48 2021-08-01    2021        8     2021-M08
#> 2: 2021/2022         49 2021-08-08    2021        8     2021-M08
#> 3: 2021/2022         50 2021-08-15    2021        8     2021-M08
synthetic_years("2021-30", "2022-10")
#>    granularity_time isoyearweek isoyear isoweek isoquarter isoyearquarter
#>              <char>      <char>   <int>   <int>      <int>         <char>
#> 1:          isoyear     2021-52    2021      52          4        2021-Q4
#> 2:          isoyear     2022-52    2022      52          4        2022-Q4
#>       season seasonweek       date calyear calmonth calyearmonth
#>       <char>      <num>     <Date>   <int>    <int>       <char>
#> 1: 2021/2022         18 2022-01-02    2022        1     2022-M01
#> 2: 2022/2023         18 2023-01-01    2023        1     2023-M01
